Subject: Post-call recap: inference evaluation — reliability, rate limits & next tests

Hi John — thanks for the call earlier. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we keep momentum: 

1) Key priorities you called out
- Uptime / SLA profile (enterprise SLAs and historical uptime)
- Rate-limit behavior under sustained and burst load (how throttling behaves and burst capacity)
- Failover characteristics (cross-region and model-variant fallback)
- Error budgets and what constitutes a breach for you (per-route vs global)

2) What Redwood will provide next (proposal)
- Short comparison matrix vs two baselines you asked about: hyperscaler managed endpoints and OtherAPI Inc.
- A focused SLO test plan: sustained load run, burst stress test, regional failover scenario, and 99/99.9 latency and error-rate reporting.
- Concrete contract/ops items for procurement (MAP + timeline).

3) Asks from your side
- Prioritized KPIs (which matters more: 99.9 latency vs absolute error-rate)
- Procurement contact and preferred PO timeline
- Any compliance checks we should run during the test (SOC2 evidence already requested in the call)

Attachments: I’ve attached a short MAP draft and a one-page SLO summary for the evaluation. I also started a comparison sheet (will share a live copy).

Proposed test window: Mar 3–5 (can be adjusted). Does that work for you?

Thanks — I’ll loop Marissa and Karthik to draft the test plan and the competitor baseline.

— Logan

Subject: Re: Post-call recap: inference evaluation — reliability, rate limits & next tests

Thanks, Logan — appreciate the clear recap. Confirming a few priorities from our side so your tests align with procurement and infra: 

- Top metrics: uptime (monthly), error rate (5xx / token), and latency p95/p99/p99.9. If you can provide historical uptime for your hosted endpoints (last 12 months) that helps procurement.
- Rate limiting: we expect a baseline of 400–600 RPS sustained on critical routes with ability to absorb ~2x bursts for short durations. We want to know exact throttling semantics (429 vs queueing) and how token costs are impacted when throttled.
- Failover: we need regional failover times and how session/streaming state is handled during a failover (e.g., ongoing streams, client retries).

Regarding competitors: please include a short baseline against AWS SageMaker endpoints and OtherAPI Inc (we already have some numbers for OtherAPI but want Redwood’s side-by-side).

Procurement: looped in procurement@datapulse.io. We aim for an evaluation PO by early April if tests look good. For the test window you suggested, Mar 3–5 looks doable. Please confirm test start times and required contacts.

John

VP Product, DataPulse

Thanks — sketching a test plan and deliverables below. I attached a short spreadsheet with SLO definitions and the competitor baseline columns.

Proposed evaluation plan (Mar 3–5):
- Day 0 (Mar 2): Canary prep — ensure synthetic traffic harness (open-source runner) is connected, confirm sample keys and telemetry export to DataPulse. Owner: Karthik.
- Day 1 (Mar 3): Sustained run — 6 hours at target RPS (baseline 500 RPS) across two routes (chat & embeddings), measure p50/p95/p99/p99.9 latency, error rate, and server-side rate-limiting events. Owner: Karthik.
- Day 2 (Mar 4): Burst stress — multiple short bursts (1–3 minutes) up to 2x–3x baseline to observe throttling behavior and token cost effects. Owner: Redwood SRE.
- Day 3 (Mar 5): Failover test — simulate region failover (primary -> secondary) while running steady traffic; verify end-to-end latency delta and stream reconnection characteristics. Owner: Marissa.

Metrics & thresholds we’ll report:
- Uptime: 99.9% target for the hosted offering; historical last-12-month uptime table (we’ll include monthly numbers).
- Error budget: suggested 0.1% monthly error budget for critical routes (i.e., <= 0.1% 5xx or 429 aggregated).
- Rate limiting: baseline sustained 500 RPS, documented burst behavior (429 semantics; backoff recommended).
- Failover target: objective — complete traffic routing to secondary within 30–60s, with reconnection guidance for streaming clients.

Deliverables by Mar 6:
- Full test report (CSV + summary PDF)
- Comparison sheet vs AWS SageMaker & OtherAPI Inc (same fixture runs where possible)
- Recommended config for production (batching, cache, quantization) to meet target cost/latency tradeoffs.

Attachments: redwood-vs-hyperscaler-slos.xlsx

Questions for Sales/procurement:
- Confirm PO timeline (John’s note: early April target)
- Confirm whether DataPulse wants on-prem/private evaluation for extra isolation (adds ~2 weeks setup)

I’ll start drafting the test harness playbook and share infra needs for the canary.

— Marissa
